narrative:
The decision to deny your law school application was primarily influenced by a prediction indicating a very high likelihood—94.7%—that you would fail the bar exam if you were to take it. This prediction is based on several key factors related to your academic performance and background.

Firstly, your performance in your first and third years of school placed you in the lowest decile compared to your peers, where the average student is performing significantly better. This suggests that your grades may not be competitive enough to indicate readiness for the challenges of the bar exam. 

Additionally, your undergraduate GPA of 3.00 is below the average of 3.23 among students who were accepted, which further raises concerns about your academic preparedness. While your family income is in the middle bracket, this factor did not significantly influence the prediction compared to your academic metrics.

The combination of these factors led to a strong indication that you may struggle with the bar exam, which is a critical requirement for law practice. Given this assessment, the admissions committee felt it was in your best interest to reconsider your application until you can strengthen your academic profile.

Moving forward, it would be beneficial for you to focus on improving your grades, perhaps by seeking additional academic support or resources. Consider retaking courses where you may have struggled or engaging in study programs that can enhance your understanding of the material. Strengthening your academic record will not only improve your chances of passing the bar exam but also enhance your future applications.
